Prevention: This virus has a huge host range so avoid planting near obviously infected crops/fields.
Control thrips (vectors) at all growth stages of the crop.
Remove weeds and volunteer host plants.
Mulch with dry grass or polythene to prevent thrips pupation.
Remove and burn old tomato plants and other host crops after harvest.
Monitoring: Numerous small, dark spots on leaves, despite the name, TSWV rarely causes a wilt.
Dark streaking of the terminal shoots.
Stunting of the plant and or one-sided growth, chlorotic rings, and patches on fruits.
Monitor thrips using blue sticky traps.
Place 8 sticky traps per 0.5 acres of land, look for thrips within the foliage and flowers.
Initiate control measures on noting 5 thrips per plant or 10% infected plants.
Direct Control: Once a plant is infected it cannot be cured and will always remain infected.
Beauveria bassiana -based products into the soil to kill pupating thrips.
Spray with lambda- cyhalothrin based products.
Restrictions: Follow instructions on product label (dosage, PHI, REI) proper pesticide waste disposal among others.
